newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Bom Dyeing sees better 2nd half.
newsitem.headline: India's Bom Dyeing sees better 2nd half.

text.p: Indian textiles and petrochemicals firm Bombay Dyeing & Manufacturing Co Ltd said on Thursday it expected to post better operating results in the second half of 1996/97 (April-March).
After a board meeting on Thursday, the company announced a sharp fall in net profit, for the first half of the year, to 223.5 million rupees from 1.03 billion rupees during the year-ago period.
Sales in the first half plunged to 4.57 billion rupees from 7.27 billion rupees during the corresponding period last year.
Bombay Dyeing attributed the fall in turnover and profit to a sharp fall in international prices of polyester inputs PTA and DMT since the third quarter of the previous year.
Bombay Dyeing is India's leading DMT manufacturer.
"Overseas PTA producers have found it advantageous to dump their surplus production in the Indian market, further aggravating the situation," it said in a statement.
The situation has eased to some extent in the last two months, Bombay Dyeing said.
"Consequently, the operations of the DMT division in the second half are expected to be better than the first half, both in respect of production and sales," it added.
"Tax provision for the half year ended September 30 is made on the applicability of the minimum alternate tax for the current year," the statement said.
